neighbours.label: A hedged or deflating evaluation: the copula or modal where a claim is being qualified as not sufficient, not always ideal, less effective, or only 'may be' (the + pole is the other side: trusted wisdom, 'knows best')
fire: It is worth remembering that the cheapest flights are not always ideal for families.
The box states the serving size, which may be 30 grams. But most people eat double that.
The function name is a bit odd but is hard to rename now.
Many hikers carry a single bottle and think they are prepared. That is not sufficient on a hot day.
Leaving the dough out overnight wouldn't ruin it, and the bread turned out fine.
However, shallow sleep is a less effective way of recovering than deep sleep.
A louder alarm is not necessarily better for heavy sleepers.
The brochure quotes a battery life which may be ten hours. But real use gives about six.
quiet: It is worth remembering that the cheapest flights leave early on Tuesdays.
The box states the serving size, and most people follow it.
The function name was chosen by the original author in 2015.
Many hikers carry two bottles and refill them at the hut.
She left the dough out overnight and baked the bread at dawn.
Deep sleep helps the body recover after a long day.
The alarm rang at six and woke the whole house.
The brochure shows a photo of the battery and the charger.

notes: Weak in probes: 'not always ideal' 0.29, 'which may be ... But' 0.27, 'a bit misleading but is hard' 0.23; rebuilt versions of the top examples ('that is not enough', 'is a less effective way') only 0.13 and 0.09. Expect this to fail; the label is a best reading of the card.
